probe.text_sample: Your Page Title Halden® Pricing Changelog Help Blog About Overview Buy Halden App Store Google Play © 2026 Halden® 2 min read October 6, 2026 Halden 2.0 and the weekly review How we designed a look back at the week that takes ten minutes, not an hour. By Marta Ruiz A weekly review is the habit almost every productivity book recommends and almost nobody keeps. The usual version asks you to go through every project, every list and every inbox, and by the third week it feels like homework. With Halden 2.0 we wanted a review that fits on a Sunday sofa with a coffee going cold. It helps that Halden only has one thing a day. A week is seven things, not seventy, so there is very little to review. Three questions, one screen The review opens on Sunday evening, or whenever you choose in Settings . It asks three things, one at a time. What got done? Your seven days, each with its one thing and the focus time it took. Done days are dark, gaps are light. What slipped? Any thing that moved more than once. Halden asks whether to keep it, shrink it or let it go. What is next week for? One sentence.
